findings.entity: secondary neon window sign left of the OPEN sign (night interior wide shots 00:18.7-00:44.9)
findings.description: A lit neon sign the same size and as steady as the 'OPEN' sign beside it reads only as a red vertical bar, an empty gap, and an 'O'. Nothing blocks it (no mullion or figure covers the gap), and it looks the same in every wide night shot. So it is a garbled, non-word sign where the context calls for real text (another 'OPEN' or a brand sign).

The bills fill much of the frame and lie still at 01:40. The '100' numerals look right, but the lettering along the top border and the serial and seal text are runs of non-word glyphs instead of 'FEDERAL RESERVE NOTE' / 'THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA'. This is a typical AI-generated currency defect. Some of it is microtext, which lowers confidence.

findings.entity: window 'OPEN' neon sign, interior vs exterior views
findings.description: From outside (00:10.167) the window neon reads 'OPEN' correctly. From inside (00:18.7-01:58) the window sign reads 'OPEN' correctly as well, not mirrored. A single-sided neon sign cannot read correctly from both sides of the glass, so the two views contradict each other.

The chrome script badge on the cab door stays in view across several seconds of a static shot. It is a string of indistinct glyphs, not a recognisable make or name. It is small and stylised, so this is low confidence.
